jobs.title: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer (m/f/d) | Integration & Automation | Full-time
jobs.jd: Help us build the future of public administration! Ayunis is a Munich-based GovTech company trusted by more than 1000 cities, municipalities and districts across the DACH region. With Ayunis Core, we are building an open-source AI platform that automates repetitive administrative work. We use cutting-edge AI and engineering tools to build cutting-edge agentic technology—both for our customers and for our own development workflows. Tasks Your role As our first Forward Deployed Engineer , you implement customer projects on Ayunis Core: you connect it to the systems our customers work with every day and build the automations that run on top of them. Our go-to-market team scopes each project with the customer; you take it from there and deliver it in direct collaboration with the customer's specialist departments and IT . You are a builder first , but not a ticket taker . Before you build, you check whether the problem is well defined and whether the planned solution actually solves it. Working closely with customers, you recognize further opportunities and feed them back. Because you are the first in this role , you also build the foundation for a team: how we deliver, what we reuse and how the next Forward Deployed Engineers get productive quickly. Your responsibilities Implement defined customer projects end to end, from technical design to production, in direct collaboration with the customer. Build connections between Ayunis Core and customer systems such as document management systems, council information systems, specialist applications and identity providers, typically as MCP servers around existing APIs. Build customer-specific agents and automations on Ayunis Core. Challenge project scopes before implementation: check that the problem is well defined, flag gaps early and propose better solutions where you see them. Work with customers' IT departments, municipal data centres and software vendors to get access, permissions and security approvals in place. Own what you deploy: reliability, monitoring and support for the integrations you build. Set up the delivery practice: project templates, reusable connectors, documentation, estimation and handover to support. Spot recurring patterns across projects and, together with Product and Engineering, turn them into marketplace integrations and platform features. Help hire and onboard future Forward Deployed Engineers. Requirements What you bring Senior experience as a software engineer building and operating production systems, ideally with TypeScript and Node.js. Hands-on experience integrating external systems: REST and SOAP APIs, OAuth/OIDC, webhooks, file-based interfaces and synchronization. Experience building with LLMs and agents, including tool calling, MCP, prompt design and evaluating results. Comfort with Docker, Linux, networking and the security basics of connecting systems across organizational boundaries. A track record of delivering projects for or with customers, including handling scope, timelines and expectations. The judgement to question a requirement when it doesn't fit the problem, and the pragmatism to ship when it does. Experience building up structure where there was none: processes, reusable tooling or a team. Fluent German ( C1 or higher! ) and good English is required. Experience with public-sector IT (e.g. DMS such as enaio or d.velop, XÖV standards, municipal data centres) is helpful but not required. Our stack TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, React, TanStack, PostgreSQL, Redis, S3-compatible storage, Docker Compose, Hetzner, GitHub Actions, OpenTelemetry and multiple LLM providers. No LangChain though – we've built our agent orchestration from the ground up. Benefits What we offer A competitive salary €2,000 annual personal development budget 30 days of holiday Significant influence over an open-source product and engineering organization Flexible working hours, hybrid work and EU workations Modern Munich office and equipment Regular team events and off-sites Public transport subsidy and Wellpass Interested? jobs.title: AI Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.jd: Appunite is moving from selling engineering hours to owning outcomes, and AI is a big part of that shift. Clients come to us with a business problem and a hunch that AI can solve it. Someone has to sit with them, figure out what’s really worth building, prove it works and get the first version into production. That’s this role. This is a hands-on engineering role, not a pre-sales one. You’ll run the technical side of discovery: workshops, stakeholder interviews and reviews of the client’s systems, data and integrations. You’ll build prototypes that answer the key questions before the client commits, then shape the solution, the estimate and the technical part of the offer. Once a project is signed, you’ll lead the first phase of delivery and hand it over to an engineer you’ve prepared to take it from there. You’ll also build the practice. That means turning real projects into our AI discovery and delivery playbook and training engineers until they can run discovery on their own. What we offer Salary: 28 500 - 35 000 PLN net/month B2B - depending on your experience Remote first approach Ownership of the service Appunite is building it’s core offer around AI coding tools as the default way of working, not an experiment Requirements 5+ years in software engineering, with regular, direct client work in recent years, including scoping or presales. You’ve designed and shipped at least one LLM-based system to production (RAG, agents, extraction or classification, assistants) used by real users. You know evals, cost, latency, guardrails and the typical failure modes. Production experience in Python or TypeScript with AI SDKs, and you’re happy to work in the client’s stack. You can work in Elixir codebases, at least with AI assistance. Claude Code, Cursor or similar tools are your everyday way of building software. You’ve technically led a client implementation, or a part of one, all the way to production. You still code every day and can build a prototype that tests a hypothesis in a day or two. You can turn a vague business problem into an architecture, a list of integrations and data sources, risks and a first estimate. You’re comfortable running workshops with non-technical stakeholders and writing short, clear recommendations for business decision-makers. You’ve onboarded, mentored or trained other engineers, or set team standards. You understand the commercial side of discovery: you can cut scope down to a first phase that’s doable and sellable, and you’ll tell a client when they shouldn’t build something. Native-level Polish and C1 English, spoken and written. What you’ll do Lead the technical side of client discovery: workshops, interviews, analysis of systems, data and integrations, feasibility and risks. Build prototypes and PoCs, mostly LLM-based, that settle key questions before the client decides to go ahead. Co-create the discovery report, the technical part of the offer and the estimate, then present the solution to the client. Technically lead the first phase of delivery while preparing an engineer to take over. Build Appunite ’s playbook for AI discovery and delivery based on real projects. Train engineers through shadowing until they can run technical discovery on their own. Run internal AI sessions and create technical materials that support sales. Take part in technical interviews for future Forward Deployed Engineers. What does the recruitment process look like? Video interview with our People Team. Technical interview with an engineers. Final check with Team Leader. The decision, after which we can say “welcome on board”. Originally posted on Himalayas

jobs.title: AI/ML Engineer
jobs.jd: Über YLAB Wir bauen die KI, die wir unseren eigenen Kindern geben würden. Kinder wachsen heute mit KI auf. Wir sorgen dafür, dass diese KI neugierig macht statt süchtig, sicher ist statt datenhungrig und für Kinder gebaut wird statt für Erwachsene. Wir sind YLAB, ein kleines KI-Lab aus Köln-Ehrenfeld. Wir entwickeln Software und Hardware aus einer Hand, vom Sprachmodell bis zum Gehäuse. Unser erstes Produkt ist Onoo, ein Lernbegleiter ohne Bildschirm für Kinder ab vier. Onoo fragt zurück, lässt raten und denkt mit. Er hat keine Kamera und kein Display, zeigt keine Werbung und verkauft keine Daten. Warum YLAB Deine Arbeit landet im Kinderzimmer, nicht in einem Dashboard. Software & Hardware: KI, App, Firmware und Gerät entstehen bei uns zusammen. Du siehst, wie aus Code etwas wird, das ein Kind in die Hand nimmt. Du arbeitest an echten offenen Fragen, zum Beispiel wie KI Kinderstimmen versteht und Fünfjährigen die Welt erklärt. Tech, Pädagogik und Forschung sitzen bei uns an einem Tisch. Ehrlichkeit statt Hochglanz: Vieles bauen wir zum ersten Mal. Wenn dich das reizt, sollten wir reden. Was wir bieten Verantwortung ab Tag eins: Du bekommst echte Themen und Probleme statt Tickets, und deine Entscheidungen haben Gewicht. Top Arbeitsmaterial: Du arbeitest mit dem Setup und den Tools, die du brauchst. Flexible Weiterbildung: Konferenz, Kurs oder Workshop – du sagst uns, was dich weiterbringt. Hybrid mit Herz: Remote, wenn du Ruhe brauchst, und im Office, wenn wir gemeinsam tüfteln. Über die Rolle Onoo hört zu, denkt mit und antwortet kindgerecht. Dahinter stecken Spracherkennung, ein kuratierter Wissensraum und eine mehrstufige Safety-Pipeline. Der Prototyp funktioniert, der Launch ist 2027. Jetzt bauen wir die Pipeline, die Millionen Kinderfragen aushält. Du bist unsere erste dedizierte AI/ML-Stelle, mit Platz am Gründertisch. Du arbeitest direkt mit Lennard (CEO, Product & AI) und entscheidest mit, wie unser Stack aussieht. Vom Modell-Routing bis zum Latenzbudget auf dem Gerät. Was dich erwartet: echte Edge-Cases wie Kinderstimmen, Dialekte und Quatschfragen, dazu harte Grenzen bei Latenz, Kosten und Datenschutz. Und die Verantwortung, dass jede Antwort sicher ist, bevor sie ein Kind erreicht. Wie du uns helfen kannst Du baust und betreibst unsere Sprach-Pipeline: Spracherkennung für Kinderstimmen, Dialogführung, Sprachausgabe. Schnell genug fürs Wohnzimmer. Du orchestrierst Sprachmodelle provider-agnostisch: Routing, Prompting, Evals, Kostenkontrolle. Du entwickelst unsere Safety-Layer weiter: Klassifikatoren, Guardrails, mehrstufige Prüfungen vor jeder Antwort. Du baust Evaluations-Sets aus echten Kinderfragen und misst, was „gut erklärt“ heißt. Du bringst Modelle in Produktion: EU-Hosting, Monitoring, Fallbacks, saubere Degradation. Du arbeitest eng mit Research und Pädagogik, damit Erkenntnisse im Produkt landen. Du hältst unseren Stack einfach. Lieber ein robuster Pfad als fünf halbe. Melde dich, wenn: Du hast 3+ Jahre ML/AI in Produktion gebracht, nicht nur in Notebooks. Du kennst dich mit LLM-Pipelines aus: Prompting, RAG, Evals, Latenz- und Kosten-Tuning. Audio/Speech (ASR/TTS) ist für dich kein Neuland. Oder du hast Lust, dich reinzubeißen. Python ist dein Zuhause und TypeScript schreckt dich nicht. Du triffst lieber Entscheidungen, als auf fertige Specs zu warten. Datenschutz und Safety sind für dich Teil des Designs, keine Checkliste. Du willst, dass deine Arbeit im Kinderzimmer ankommt und nicht im Backlog. Eher nicht, wenn: du nur Modelle trainieren willst und Produktion dich langweilt. Oder wenn du erst loslegst, wenn Anforderungen, Team und Prozesse fertig sind. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

jobs.title: Lead Data Scientist, Revenue - Ads, Revenue
jobs.jd:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third.
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

Vinted’s Revenue domain is growing — Ads business is on the mission to develop an advertising ecosystem within Vinted and we’re just getting started. We’re looking for a Lead Data Scientist to join our cross-functional team in Ads to help us make the most of our real estate and evolve toward a high‑performance, privacy‑respectful, in‑house advertising ecosystem over time. Think: an ad of an external partner can generate euros directly but we may well advertise our own Marketplace services or newly launched categories to optimise on net revenue as well as user engagement. 

If you have built performance-first Ad optimisation systems and are ready to take on hands-on work while shaping the Data Science roadmaps from a greenfield state - this role is for you.

In this position, you’ll 

  • Own optimization logic for Ads systems. Own the data science approach behind core Ads optimization problems such as ranking, targeting, pacing, budget allocation, candidate selection, and auction or bidding logic where relevant.
  • Develop practical approaches that improve advertiser performance, marketplace relevance, and business outcomes.
  • Take charge of model and algorithm development. Design, develop, and iterate models and algorithmic approaches used in Ads delivery and optimization. This may include prediction, scoring, calibration, exploration/exploitation methods, and constrained optimization approaches suited to Vinted’s marketplace context.
  • Lead experimentation and performance improvement frameworks. Own the analytical and experimental process for improving optimization systems. Define hypotheses, evaluation frameworks or logic changes and support translating learnings into better system behavior.
  • Guide objective function and constraint design. Help define optimization objectives that balance advertiser value, revenue, user experience, and operational constraints. Turn product and business goals into tractable optimization problems and implementable Data Science logic.
  • Be responsible for Ads performance diagnostics. Own deep-dive analysis of system behavior and performance degradation. Identify where delivery, relevance, auction dynamics, supply-demand imbalance, or model issues are limiting outcomes, and propose solutions.
  • Contribute to Production implementation in Ads. Partner with engineering and Decision Scientists to move models and optimization logic from idea to reliable implementation.
  • Partner with Product Managers, Decision Scientists, Analytics Engineers and developers to shape advertiser-facing features and internal optimization capabilities with a clear understanding of feasibility, impact, and tradeoffs from the Data Science perspective.
  • Collaborate with Decision Science counterparts and other Data Scientists to ensure optimization changes are evaluated with appropriate metrics, guardrails, and marketplace context.
  • Partner with Analytics Engineering, Data Engineering, and backend teams to ensure training data, feedback loops, online signals, and offline datasets are suitable for robust optimization work.
  • Help explain system behavior, performance drivers, and expected impacts of optimization changes to non-technical stakeholders when needed.

About you 

We are looking for someone who combines:

  • strong applied machine learning and statistical skills,
  • experience with Ad Tech systems and optimization problems,
  • strong product and business judgment,
  • comfort working on production systems with engineers,
  • and the ability to operate effectively in ambiguous, evolving domains.

jobs.jd: Location: San Francisco or Singapore (on-site), or remote (Singapore or US Pacific time zones) Start Date: ASAP Languages: English Team: Engineering About the Role Our client is a fast-growing AI company building reliable, fair and open infrastructure for AI training data. Their marketplace helps the people who create data get value for it, and gives AI labs trustworthy data to train on. It is already used by startups, Fortune 500 companies and frontier labs, and the company is backed by leading venture investors, including Y Combinator. They are scaling quickly to meet strong demand. We are looking for a Research Engineer, Privacy and Anonymization to build the systems that make sensitive, real-world data safe and still useful for AI training. You will develop methods to detect and remove personally identifiable information, secrets and other sensitive content from raw data before it enters processing and synthetic data pipelines â protecting privacy without destroying the structure and signal that make the data valuable for training agents. This is a privacy and data-protection engineering seat, not a synthetic-task design role. You will own the pipeline that stands in front of downstream processing, training, evaluation and synthetic generation. This is a full-time role, starting ASAP. Offices are in San Francisco and Singapore; remote candidates are welcome if their working hours can overlap about 70â80% with either San Francisco (US Pacific) or Singapore business hours. The exact daily schedule will be agreed during hiring. What You'll Do Build systems to detect PII, quasi-identifiers, credentials and other sensitive information, and design transformations based on the data type and the downstream use case. Develop and benchmark detection approaches that combine rules, statistical models, classifiers and LLM-based methods. Build production pipelines that anonymize raw data before it enters downstream processing, training, evaluation or synthetic data generation. Create evaluation frameworks that measure privacy risk and retained data utility, including recall-weighted metrics, leakage tests and adversarial re-identification attempts. Design systems that stay robust to new data sources, schema drift, unusual formats and sensitive information embedded in unexpected fields. Work with engineering, research, operations and customers to translate privacy requirements into practical technical policies and safeguards. Experience with information extraction, named-entity recognition, classification, or related methods for detecting rare or sensitive content. Strong experimental instincts, and the ability to compare approaches across recall, precision, latency, cost and downstream data utility. An understanding of the difference between redaction, masking, pseudonymization, anonymization and synthetic data â and when each is appropriate. High attention to detail, and the ability to reason about subtle leakage paths, edge cases and adversarial failure modes. Experience building data-processing pipelines end to end, including where there was no fully prescribed roadmap. Clear written and spoken English, and comfort collaborating across teams and time zones. Strong candidates may also have hands-on experience with privacy-enhancing technologies (such as differential privacy, k-anonymity, secure aggregation or format-preserving encryption); have worked with sensitive data in healthcare, finance or security; have built low-latency or high-throughput ML inference or data-processing systems; or have taken work from early research through to production. Technical aptitude and learning potential matter more than years of experience. Motivated candidates are encouraged to apply even if they don't meet every point above. Why This Role Matters for You Make real-world data safe to train on: You will build the systems that let sensitive data be used for AI training without exposing people or secrets. Privacy without wrecking utility: The job is not only to redact, but to keep the structure and signal that downstream training and synthetic pipelines need. From detection to production: You will own the full path: detection methods, transformations, evaluation, and the pipeline that sits in front of training and generation. Hard, high-stakes edge cases: Work on leakage paths, schema drift and adversarial failure modes, not only clean benchmark datasets. jobs.title: Senior Engineer, Machine Learning
jobs.jd: An Introduction to Primer Primer is the unified infrastructure for global payments. We give finance and payments teams the visibility and control to reduce complexity, improve performance, and capture more revenue - all from a single platform. Backed by Sofina, Peak XV Partners, ICONIQ, Tencent, Accel, and Balderton, we're building the payments layer the world's best companies rely on. Watch our showcase > Read up on our $100m Series C Learn more about our culture > Which team will you be joining? You'll be our first Senior Engineer in ML, working alongside our Staff Engineer to help build the foundations from the ground up. There's no existing DS/ML team yet, so the two of you will shape it together, working closely with engineering, data, and product, who are already exploring how ML can be used in payments. There's a lot still to figure out and a lot to build. You'll work closely with your team's stakeholders to identify where ML can move the needle, and report to engineering leadership while that function takes shape. What will you be doing? Own the full lifecycle of ML-powered features within your initiatives - from independently researching and testing approaches through training, deployment and monitoring in production Productionise smart routing decisions across the payment flow, building the ML infrastructure around them as you go - versioning, CI/CD, observability Partner closely with product, data and engineering to turn promising use cases into shipped, measured outcomes Bring a pragmatic, impact-first mindset to experimentation and model evaluation, rather than chasing the most sophisticated approach Mentor other engineers as they pick up ML techniques, sharing how you think about tradeoffs and when to keep things simple Talk directly to customers to validate ideas and pressure-test what you're building against real usage Help set technical direction within your area, working with your team to prioritise the use cases worth pursuing Establish patterns and practices that make ML work reliable and repeatable at Primer, building on foundations rather than defining them alone What we're looking for Senior experience in ML engineering, data science, or applied research, with real production deployments behind you (API, batch, or streaming) You think statistically. You can design and run experiments and A/B tests, and report what the results do and don't show Strong Python skills and hands-on experience with ML libraries such as scikit-learn, XGBoost, TensorFlow, PyTorch or Keras Solid grounding in modern software engineering, infrastructure and data tooling, and an understanding of the MLOps challenges across the full ML lifecycle. You don't need to have built a platform, but you know what one has to handle Familiarity with reinforcement learning (multi-armed or contextual bandits, for example). Production experience with it isn't required, but you need to understand how it works and where it applies Cloud experience — AWS preferred; GCP or Azure both fine Exposure to payments or e-commerce is a plus, not a prerequisite - you'll build that domain depth on the job Comfortable with ambiguity, in the problems and in the process. You can research, develop and productionise independently, and you'll help define how we work as you go You may not like it here You enjoy working in an office setting — we're remote-first, and always will be You need a fully mapped-out roadmap before you start — we're building this function, and there is a lot yet to be defined. You prefer handing models to another team to deploy and run. ✅ A typical interview process An initial intro call with a Talent Partner An interview with the Hiring Manager Challenge Stage - Contextualised to the role A final, values-alignment interview What's the culture like at Primer? We're building a culture where people can do their best work and be proud of the impact they have. You'll be working with people who are mission-driven, smart, and reflective, and who are genuinely invested in building exceptional products and delivering success for our merchants. We work remotely, and have done since day one. We believe that building a successful, profitable company goes beyond proximity. We invest in our relationships through great remote working practices and thoughtfully designed face-to-face time, including workations, our annual company retreat, and access to co-working spaces across most major cities. The work is challenging. Scaleups are a challenge, and building category-defining products is a challenge. But there's a meaningful difference between a challenge and a struggle. At Primer, the right challenge comes with the right support: strong onboarding, a collaborative environment, and a team that is genuinely invested in your success. It's never something you face alone. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Finance Technology (Forward Deployed)
jobs.jd: Position Summary Vista Equity Partners is seeking a Senior Software Engineer to serve as the forward deployed engineer for thefirm's Finance organization. This individual contributor role, at the Associate level, sits on Enterprise AI & Automation and reports to the Director, AI Solutions Engineering, but works embedded day to day with the Finance Technology team. The engineer learns how Finance works, finds the problems worth solving, and ships production software on Vista's AI platform, from treasury and close tooling to AI experiences over curated finance data. They also partner with the technologists already building inside Finance, so that what the department builds meets platform standards and can run in production. The team works primarily in TypeScript, Node.js, and Reacton Azure, using modern AI tooling throughout the development workflow. This role can be fully remote within the US or based in our Austin office. Responsibilities Embed with Finance as its dedicated engineer: join the team's working rhythms, learn its workflows across areas such as fund accounting, treasury, tax, and the financial close, and build trust with finance stakeholders. Turn loosely defined finance problems into product requirements and design documents, and break the workinto deliverable pieces. Design, build, and operate finance applications, automations, and AI experiences end to end on Vista's platform, integrating systems such as Snowflake, SharePoint, and Smartsheet. Partner with Finance Technology's department technologists: share platform capabilities and patterns,review their code and designs, pair on harder problems, and help their work plug into platform standards instead of running in parallel. Bring the most useful finance apps built by business users (for example, in Replit) onto Vista's enterprise platform, up to its security, SDLC, and operational standards. Lead user testing, rollouts, and go-lives with finance owners, managing scope, tradeoffs, status, and adoption directly. Own shipped software, including releases, defects, and ongoing iteration, with the accuracy, auditability, and data security that financial workflows require. Bring Finance's needs back to Enterprise AI & Automation, flagging platform gaps and reusable patterns witha recommendation. Use modern AI tooling throughout delivery while holding all shipped code to a high bar of review and quality. Participate in on-call rotation for production applications and platform services. Qualifications Technical Skills 6+ years of software engineering experience, or equivalent demonstrated scope. Production experience with TypeScript and Node.js, including designing and operating APIs. Track record of owning software in production after launch, including support, defects, and iteration. Strong SQL and experience building on a cloud data warehouse (Snowflake preferred), including access controls and data quality checks. Cloud-native delivery on a major cloud platform (Azure preferred), including infrastructure as code, CI/CD,identity, and observability. Established AI-native engineering practice, using AI coding tools well beyond autocomplete to ship production software. Degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent experience. Domain Knowledge Working familiarity with private equity finance, such as fund structures, capital calls and distributions,management fees and carried interest, fund accounting, and investor reporting. Deep expertise is not required. Comfort learning finance workflows quickly and speaking the language of accountants, controllers, and treasury teams. Soft Skills Excellent written and verbal communication, including explaining technical tradeoffs to finance leaders. Enjoys working inside a business team: listens first, learns the work, and earns trust by shipping. Product mindset, with experience taking a product or feature set from zero to adoption and understanding the business reasons behind the code. Experience working directly with non-technical stakeholders on requirements, tradeoffs, and rollouts. Collaborative mindset, with the ability to raise the work of technical colleagues outside engineering through review and pairing. Comfortable with ambiguity, change, and a high degree of autonomy. Forward deployed, solutions engineering, or other customer-embedded engineering experience. Experience with fund accounting, treasury, or ERP systems and their APIs. Experience supporting or governing citizen developer or low-code populations. React or Terraform. Actual base pay could vary based on factors including but not limited to experience, subject matter expertise, geographic location where work will be performed and the applicant’s skill set. The base pay is just one component of the total compensation package for employees. Other components may include an annual cash bonus and a comprehensive benefits package. For over 25 years and across every technology cycle, Vista has been pioneering new approaches to software investing, delivering consistent and compelling results at scale. Today, we're applying that expertise to help harness the transformative potential of AI to redefine how work gets done. Further information is available at vistaequitypartners.com. jobs.title: AI/ML Researcher
jobs.jd: Über YLAB Wir bauen die KI, die wir unseren eigenen Kindern geben würden. Kinder wachsen heute mit KI auf. Wir sorgen dafür, dass diese KI neugierig macht statt süchtig, sicher ist statt datenhungrig und für Kinder gebaut wird statt für Erwachsene. Wir sind YLAB, ein kleines KI-Lab aus Köln-Ehrenfeld. Wir entwickeln Software und Hardware aus einer Hand, vom Sprachmodell bis zum Gehäuse. Unser erstes Produkt ist Onoo, ein Lernbegleiter ohne Bildschirm für Kinder ab vier. Onoo fragt zurück, lässt raten und denkt mit. Er hat keine Kamera und kein Display, zeigt keine Werbung und verkauft keine Daten. Warum YLAB Deine Arbeit landet im Kinderzimmer, nicht in einem Dashboard. Software & Hardware: KI, App, Firmware und Gerät entstehen bei uns zusammen. Du siehst, wie aus Code etwas wird, das ein Kind in die Hand nimmt. Du arbeitest an echten offenen Fragen, zum Beispiel wie KI Kinderstimmen versteht und Fünfjährigen die Welt erklärt. Tech, Pädagogik und Forschung sitzen bei uns an einem Tisch. Ehrlichkeit statt Hochglanz: Vieles bauen wir zum ersten Mal. Wenn dich das reizt, sollten wir reden. Was wir bieten Verantwortung ab Tag eins: Du bekommst echte Themen und Probleme statt Tickets, und deine Entscheidungen haben Gewicht. Top Arbeitsmaterial: Du arbeitest mit dem Setup und den Tools, die du brauchst. Flexible Weiterbildung: Konferenz, Kurs oder Workshop – du sagst uns, was dich weiterbringt. Hybrid mit Herz: Remote, wenn du Ruhe brauchst, und im Office, wenn wir gemeinsam tüfteln. Über die Rolle Wie versteht ein Sprachmodell eine Vierjährige? Und wie erklärt es ihr die Welt, ohne sie zu überfordern? Dazu gibt es kaum Paper und keine Benchmarks. Genau da setzt du an. Du bist unsere erste dedizierte Research-Stelle. Du arbeitest an der Schnittstelle von KI, Sprache und Pädagogik, mit echten Familien statt Laborbedingungen und mit direktem Draht ins Produkt. Was dich erwartet: offene Fragen mit Substanz, ein Fachbeirat aus Bildung und Psychologie und die Freiheit, Studien so zu bauen, wie sie sein müssen. Wie du uns helfen kannst Du entwirfst und machst Studien mit Kindern und Familien. Von der Beobachtung im Wohnzimmer bis zum strukturierten Test. Du baust Methoden, um altersgerechte Antworten zu bewerten: Was heißt verständlich, was heißt zu viel? Du übersetzt Erkenntnisse in Modell- und Produktentscheidungen, zusammen mit Engineering und Pädagogik. Du behältst die Forschung im Blick (Child-Computer Interaction, Speech, LLM-Evals) und holst rein, was uns weiterbringt. Du teilst, was wir lernen. Wir forschen nicht für die Schublade. Melde dich, wenn: Du hast einen Research-Hintergrund, etwa HCI, Psychologie, Linguistik oder ML. Du hast schon mit Nutzer:innen geforscht, am besten mit Kindern. Du kannst beides: Interviews auswerten und saubere Metriken bauen. Du schreibst klar. Für Paper genauso wie für Produktentscheidungen. Du magst es, wenn deine Forschung nächste Woche im Prototyp steckt. Eher nicht, wenn: du Forschung als Selbstzweck siehst oder zwei Jahre Vorlauf brauchst, bevor etwas testbar ist. jobs.title: Applied AI Engineer, Codex
jobs.jd: About the Team OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. For software engineering organizations, this means helping customers adopt Codex and other OpenAI capabilities across the software development lifecycle—transforming how teams plan, build, test, review, and deliver software. We work directly with engineering leaders and hands-on developers to identify high-value opportunities, design and implement AI-powered development workflows, and scale what works across engineering organizations. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products, reusable architectures, and technical patterns that help developers everywhere get more value from Codex. About the Role As an Applied AI Engineer focused on Codex, you will partner directly with leading engineering organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that transform how software is developed. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from workflow and use-case selection through prototyping, evaluation, production rollout, and scaled adoption. You will work alongside engineering teams to build advanced AI coding workflows, integrations, automations, and evaluation systems—often using Codex itself as part of your development process. You will help customers make technical decisions involving model behavior, agentic workflows, developer environments, security, reliability, evaluation, and operational readiness, while ensuring deployments translate into measurable improvements in engineering productivity and software delivery. You will work closely with OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, Sales, and the broader Codex organization, translating real-world deployment experience into high-signal product and model feedback. Success is measured by production systems, sustained developer adoption, and meaningful improvements to how engineering organizations build software—not simply successful demonstrations or enablement activity. This role is based in our Munich office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: Partner directly with engineering leaders and hands-on developers to identify high-value opportunities for Codex and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria. Design, build, and deploy AI-powered software development workflows that improve how engineering teams plan, write, test, review, debug, and deliver software. Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, workflow automations, and production accelerators—often using Codex as part of your own development process. Help customers progress from promising experiments to reliable production workflows, sustained developer adoption, and scaled impact across engineering organizations. Design systematic approaches for evaluating AI coding systems using representative software engineering tasks, automated graders, production signals, and developer feedback. Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, tools, developer environments, integrations, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and operational readiness. Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive technical blockers toward resolution. Lead technical deep dives, workshops, and hands-on enablement that help engineering teams understand and adopt advanced AI coding workflows effectively and safely. Gather high-fidelity insights from real-world Codex deployments and translate them into clear product proposals, model feedback, and technical requirements for OpenAI Product, Research, and Engineering teams. Create reusable architectures, tooling, examples, guides, and technical patterns—including contributions to resources such as the OpenAI Cookbook—that accelerate future Codex deployments. Influence customer engineering strategy by helping technical leaders understand how AI coding systems can reshape their software development lifecycle, engineering practices, and organizational workflows. You’ll thrive in this role if you: Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering software or AI systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, developer tooling, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting. Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, integrations, or production engineering—not only program, enablement, or stakeholder management. Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across modern software development environments; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable. Are an active user of AI coding tools and have developed a strong point of view on how AI can improve developer productivity and software engineering workflows. Enjoy building high-signal prototypes, integrations, automations, and production solutions that demonstrate and deliver what AI coding systems can enable. Understand how to evaluate AI coding systems systematically, including designing representative tasks, automated evaluations, production signals, and mechanisms for incorporating developer feedback. Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as developer tooling integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost. Can connect technical decisions to developer workflows, adoption, engineering productivity, and measurable business outcomes. Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, eng

Nobody checks every box - we’re looking for candidates that are particularly strong in a few areas, and have some interest and capabilities in others. About the Role: We are seeking a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to join Kong’s growing Professional Services organization. This is a highly strategic, customer-facing engineering role focused on helping enterprise customers accelerate adoption of Kong’s API and AI Connectivity platform through hands-on implementation, automation, migration tooling, and solution engineering. As an FDE, you will work directly alongside customer engineering teams to solve complex technical challenges, accelerate migrations, build reusable automation, and deliver production-grade solutions in real-world enterprise environments. You will operate at the intersection of software engineering, architecture, platform engineering, and customer delivery. This role is ideal for engineers who enjoy building, coding, solving ambiguous problems, and working directly with customers on mission-critical initiatives involving APIs, AI gateways, service connectivity, modernization, and cloud-native platforms. You will collaborate closely with Solutions Architects, Engagement Managers, Product Engineering, Customer Success, and Product teams to ensure successful customer outcomes while also influencing Kong’s product direction based on field experience. Working at Kong is a unique opportunity to make a massive impact on Fortune 50/500 customers as they modernize mission-critical systems for the AI era. What’s in it for you? Impact Work directly with some of the world’s largest enterprises to modernize API infrastructure and accelerate AI adoption through Kong’s connectivity platform. Growth Accelerate your technical and professional growth through exposure to cutting-edge cloud-native technologies, distributed systems, AI connectivity, automation frameworks, and large-scale enterprise architectures. Opportunity Be part of a rapidly growing Professional Services organization that is shaping how enterprises adopt APIs, AI gateways, and modern connectivity platforms globally. What You’ll Do: Partner directly with enterprise customers to design, build, and implement Kong-based solutions across cloud, hybrid, and on-premise environments. Lead hands-on implementation efforts for API gateways, AI gateways, service mesh, developer portals, and related connectivity technologies. Build automation frameworks, migration tooling, custom integrations, and reusable accelerators to simplify customer adoption and modernization efforts. jobs.title: Advisory Solution Consultant - CRM & Agentic AI
jobs.jd: As an Advisory Solution Consultant - CRM & Agentic AI for the Switzerland market, you are the technical face of a fundamentally different way of selling. Rather than leading with slideware and scripted demos, you embed alongside the customer, run deep Discovery to isolate one high-value problem, and then prove value in the open — building a working Proof of Value (POV) on the customer’s own data using our Agentic workflow capabilities. You partner with Sales, Product Management, and Executive Leadership to turn a single, well-chosen use case into undeniable, data-backed proof that earns the next phase of the relationship. This role blends the consultative instincts of a Sr. Advisory Solution Consultant with the hands-on, build-it-in-the-field engineering of a forward-deployed engineer: someone who works inside the customer’s own environment, configuring and proving solutions on their live data rather than presenting finished products from the outside. The Embedded Approach The Advisory Solution Consultant inverts the traditional pre-sales motion. Product demonstration is deliberately minimal — just enough to establish credibility and unlock the real work. The center of gravity is the POV: a short, focused cycle where we get access to a slice of the customer’s data, stand up an Agentic workflow against a problem they genuinely care about, and let the outcome speak for itself. Your job is to earn the right to that POV through rigorous Discovery, then deliver it as an embedded engineer, not a presenter. What You’ll Do As the Advisory Solution Consultant, you will lead a Discovery-first, POV-centric engagement model — using your technical depth and Agentic workflow expertise to convert customer data into proven outcomes, while supporting quarterly and annual sales objectives for your region. Key responsibilities include: Partner with Sales as the embedded technical lead — someone who wins on proof, not presentation — to drive transformational CRM opportunities. Lead rigorous Discovery to isolate a single, high-value problem worth solving, mapping the customer’s data, systems, and desired outcome before any product is shown. Keep product demonstration minimal and purposeful — use it only to establish credibility and to set up the POV, never as a substitute for proving value on real data. Secure and scope a POV: earn customer sponsorship to engage in a hands-on cycle where we use their data to solve the identified problem with our Agentic workflow capabilities. Build and deliver the POV as an embedded engineer — configuring Agentic workflows against the customer’s environment and producing measurable, data-backed results. Translate POV outcomes into an executive value narrative that quantifies impact and defines the path from a single proven use case to enterprise-wide adoption. jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Transaction Risk
jobs.jd:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Transaction Risk team builds the machine learning systems behind Stripe Radar, helping businesses prevent fraud and abuse while letting legitimate customers through. We combine intelligence from across Stripe’s global network with real-time models and AI agents to protect businesses across the customer lifecycle, from signup and free trials to payments and ongoing usage, with a growing focus on the emerging threats facing AI companies.

The team is growing, and expanding into multiple new areas. We are building abuse protections across the full customer life-cycle and solving emerging token fraud problems to make Stripe the default fraud and abuse solution for AI.

What you’ll do

You will own major ML systems and initiatives from problem definition to production. You'll find where ML can make the biggest difference, design the approach, build and ship models and the systems around them, and keep improving them as data, users, and attackers change.

Your work may include protecting businesses from abuse across the customer lifecycle, building adaptive and customizable fraud systems for Stripe's largest users, or extending risk intelligence to 50+ global payment methods. Across all of these, you'll use modern approaches, such as transformer models over payment data, graph intelligence across consumers, and LLMs that detect emerging attacks. 

You will have opportunities to ship 0→1 products, and to improve mission-critical ML models operating at Stripe scale, often driving several efforts in parallel and setting the technical bar for the team.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the design and delivery of ML projects end to end, from framing the problem and sizing the opportunity through deployment, monitoring, and iteration.
  • Build, train, evaluate, and deploy models that detect fraud and abuse across Stripe’s global network, and own the production systems they run on.
  • Investigate emerging fraud and abuse patterns, decide where ML can have the most impact, and quickly turn those insights into shipped protections.
  • Design features, datasets, and evaluation strategies for noisy, delayed, and adversarial environments, and set the bar for experimental rigor.
  • Make sound architecture and modeling tradeoffs between model quality, legitimate-user impact, latency, reliability, and operational cost.
  • Be the go-to expert for the systems you own: lead incident response for model regressions, reduce operational toil, and make your systems easy for others to build on.
  • Partner with engineering, product, data science, risk experts, and leading Stripe users to turn modeling improvements into differentiated Radar products.
  • Turn recurring problems into reusable components, tools, and AI-assisted workflows that speed up the whole team.
  • Mentor engineers, give thoughtful design and code reviews, and help new teammates ramp up quickly.

Who you are

You are an experienced ML engineer who combines deep modeling expertise with strong engineering judgment. You've owned ML systems in production, shipped multiple meaningful improvements, and made the people around you more effective. You move fast without breaking things, you're comfortable leading through ambiguity, and you're excited to work at the frontier of payments and AI, turning advances in machine learning into production systems that address new forms of fraud and abuse.

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of experience developing, evaluating, and deploying machine learning models in a production environment.
  • A track record of leading ML projects from problem definition to production, with measurable impact.
  • Deep foundations in machine learning, statistics, model evaluation, and experiment design.
  • Strong programming and software-engineering skills, with experience writing tested, maintainable code for production ML applications.
  • Experience designing and operating production ML systems, including several of: large-scale data and feature pipelines, distributed model training, low-latency inference, model deployment, or production monitoring.
  • Experience mentoring engineers or technically leading projects with multiple contributors.
  • Ability to investigate ambiguous problems, reason from data, and choose pragmatic technical approaches.
  • Ability to communicate technical ideas and results clearly and collaborate effectively across disciplines.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience applying ML to fraud detection, integrity, trust and safety, identity, cybersecurity, or another adversarial domain.
  • Experience developing or productionizing modern deep learning, graph-learning, or LLM-based approaches.
  • Experience building and optimizing real-time, low-latency ML systems at scale.
  • Experience owning the operational health of critical ML systems, including on-call, incident response, and migrations.
  • Experience rapidly building 0→1 products or wor

jobs.title: Senior Generative AI Engineer
jobs.jd: About Motorway Motorway is the UK's largest online car-selling platform. We connect private sellers directly with over 8,000 dealers nationwide. Our online platform helps sellers achieve great prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want for their dealerships. Founded in 2017, our award-winning, technology-led approach has redefined the experience of selling a car. Motorway is backed by some of the world’s leading technology investors, having raised £143 million in Series C funding. This is a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing scale-up at a crucial phase of growth and help change an industry for the better. About the team GenAI Engineering sits within Motorway's Data and AI function, alongside Machine Learning and the Machine Learning Data Platform. We own the AI features that shape how buyers and sellers experience the marketplace, from agentic workflows in the customer journey to LLM-powered tooling for our dealer network. What we build goes into the hands of real sellers and thousands of verified dealers, usually within weeks. When it works, someone sells their car more easily. When it doesn't, we hear about it. That feedback loop is short, and it shapes how we work. We have a track record of successful deployments and a strong reputation as a result. About the role We're looking for a Senior GenAI Engineer to build AI applications and agentic workflows for Motorway, taking them from rapid prototype through to production-grade systems that deliver measurable value. You'll take a problem that isn't fully defined yet and see it through to a reliable system running in production: the prompting, the retrieval, the agent design, the evals, the guardrails, the monitoring. You own that whole stack. There's no separate team who "productionises" your work later. Most of what makes a GenAI feature good sits around the model rather than in it. The prompting is rarely the hard part. Retrieval quality is, and so is the data feeding it, evaluation you can trust, sensible behaviour when things fail, and getting it live and keeping it there. If that's the work you want to do, we're not precious about the route you took to get here. Some of us came through data science and machine learning and deliberately built up our software engineering; others came the other way. In this role, you will: Own AI features end to end, from an ambiguous problem through to a reliable, observable system that real customers depend on. Build the retrieval and data foundations these features stand on, and treat retrieval quality as a first-class engineering problem rather than a tuning exercise. Design evaluation and monitoring approaches that make quality, reliability and safety measurable rather than assumed. Build AI applications and agents using LLMs, orchestration, APIs and data systems, applying solid production software practices throughout. Make the calls on models, cost and latency that shape what a feature costs us to run, and document the reasoning so others can follow it. Prototype quickly, work out what is reusable, and harden the patterns that work into components the rest of the team adopts. Raise the quality of the work around you through code review, design feedback and the standards you set by example. Represent your technical decisions directly to product managers and stakeholders, translating model behaviour into business consequence. About you You've shipped AI or ML systems that real users depend on, and you've stayed close enough to production to know how they behave when they break. Strong Python, and SQL you genuinely use. A lot of this work is data work: assembling grounding data, building golden datasets, and digging into why something failed. You've invested deliberately in your software engineering craft: testing, error handling, CI/CD, observability, and the MLOps practices that keep things healthy once they're live. You're hands-on across the GenAI stack: LLM APIs, retrieval and vector stores, agents with tool use, and structured outputs, running on cloud infrastructure (we use AWS and GCP). You have a real point of view on evaluation, most likely because you've been caught out by a system that looked fine and wasn't. You can reason about how models fail, including hallucination and prompt injection, and what that means for someone who trusts the output. You know when to reach for a model, when something simpler will do, and when to stop. You're a constructive reviewer, and colleagues are better off for having worked alongside you. You could be a great fit if You're curious about how things actually work, and you follow that curiosity past the first plausible answer. You're drawn to problems where the right approach isn't obvious yet. You're honest about the limits of what you know and pull people in early rather than late. You take responsibility for what you ship, watch how it behaves, and fix it when it breaks. You get satisfaction from the unglamorous work that makes an AI feature actually good, not just the part that demos well. You can disagree well, and commit once a decision is made. Benefits We've got your back, in life's biggest moments and the everyday ones too. Competitive salary Equity scheme - we all share in Motorway's success 25 days holiday Flexible working (2 days a week in our London office, with socials and snacks galore) Private medical insurance via BUPA Life assurance Pension scheme (we contribute 5%) Enhanced family leave (e.g. 26 weeks full pay for maternity or adoption) 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme EV leasing scheme Cycle to work scheme Nursery salary sacrifice scheme 1 paid volunteering day a year Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

Build the hardest pieces of work directly, acting as the technical escalation point for the function's toughest problems. Design for systems that stay up and stay affordable, covering graceful degradation, fallback behaviour, and cost and latency at production scale. Develop the senior engineers around you by handing them harder problems, room to own decisions, and honest feedback. Shape how we hire and review, bringing a clear and defensible view of what good looks like. Bring specific, actionable industry insight into planning, explaining what a development means for our architecture rather than noting that the field moves fast. About you You've set technical direction that other engineering teams actually adopted, and you can talk about where that worked and where it didn't. Strong Python, and SQL you genuinely use. A lot of this work is data work: grounding data, golden datasets, and understanding why something failed. Deep, current expertise across the GenAI stack, including retrieval at scale, vector stores, agentic orchestration, multimodal work, evaluation infrastructure and fine-tuning where it earns its place. You're fluent in the layer underneath: MLOps tooling, deployment and cloud infrastructure (we run on AWS and GCP), and you can tell the difference between a choice that matters and one that doesn't. You design systems that survive contact with production, and you've been on the hook when they didn't. A strong point of view on evaluation, including the difference between evals that catch regressions and evals that provide comfort. Your direct contributions set a quality bar for the people around you. You explain hard technical trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders without either condescending or losing the substance. Self-awareness about where your knowledge runs out, and the instinct to bring in expertise early. You could be a great fit if You build with taste, preferring simple systems that work over clever ones that nearly do. You use authority sparingly. You're not a blocker, but you'll stop a bad decision from shipping. You get satisfaction from the unglamorous work that makes AI features actually good, not just the part that demos well. jobs.title: CDI - Senior AI Engineer - Paris
jobs.jd:
Mission

De nouveaux modèles, ouverts ou fermés, sortent chaque mois : encore faut-il choisir ceux qui sont assez bons pour la production, et le démontrer. Applications et agents s’appuient sur les grands modèles de langage (LLM), et la partie modèle de ces systèmes est entre vos mains. Nos clients s’en servent pour répondre à leurs propres clients, traiter des documents et interroger leurs connaissances.

Ce que le modèle voit, la manière dont il retrouve les connaissances, les outils qu’il peut appeler : ces choix vous appartiennent, de même que la mesure de la qualité des réponses. Le modèle retenu doit tenir l’objectif de coût et de qualité.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez savoir si un système d’IA donne des réponses justes, et pas seulement s’il tourne.

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype AI Engineer.

 

Activités et responsabilités

Les Product Engineers construisent l’application autour du modèle ; le comportement du modèle à l’intérieur vous revient. Les Context & Analytics Engineers préparent les connaissances que vos agents retrouvent, et les Platform Engineers exploitent le serving, le harness et l’observabilité sur lesquels vous vous appuyez.

Avec l’AI Product Manager et les experts métier du client, une bonne réponse se définit, puis les résultats s’examinent ensemble. La relecture de code entre pairs et l’accompagnement des nouvelles recrues font partie du quotidien.

Vos responsabilités :

  • Construire des applications et des agents LLM : conception du contexte, appel d’outils, workflows multi-étapes.
  • Concevoir la façon dont les agents exploitent les connaissances : requêtes de retrieval, re-ranking, citations.
  • Construire des jeux et des pipelines d’évaluation : réponses de référence, scoring automatisé, relecture par des experts métier.
  • Suivre la qualité des réponses en production et corriger ce qui se dégrade.
  • Choisir les modèles selon la qualité, le coût et la latence ; faire du fine-tuning ou de la distillation sur un modèle plus petit quand le prompting ne suffit pas.
  • Ajouter des garde-fous contre les mauvaises réponses, les fuites de données et le prompt injection.
  • Traiter des documents avec des LLM : extraction, classification, résumés.

 

Profil recherché

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous avez construit une application ou un agent qui appelle un LLM, et vous savez expliquer ce qui a fonctionné et ce qui a échoué.
  2. Votre code est testé et maintenable.
  3. Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.
  4. La qualité des sorties d’IA se mesure chez vous avec des jeux de test et des métriques, et vous savez limiter les hallucinations, le prompt injection et les fuites de données.
  5. Mettre en production une application LLM et la maintenir (déploiement, monitoring, coût, latence) n’a pas de secret pour vous.
  6. Le point de départ, pour vous, est le problème métier plutôt que le modèle ; reconnaître que l’IA n’est pas toujours le bon outil, et l’expliquer à des personnes non techniques, fait partie de votre pratique.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Du fine-tuning ou de la distillation de modèles de langage.
  • Une formation en machine learning ou en statistiques, par exemple en data science.
  • Des frameworks ou des protocoles d’agents, comme MCP.
  • Des entrées multimodales : documents, images, voix.
  • Des outils d’observabilité LLM : tracing, suivi des coûts.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

 

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Dans ce métier, la difficulté est moins de faire parler un modèle que de savoir s’il dit juste. L’AI Engineer répond à cette question par la mesure : jeux de test, évaluations, suivi en production, plutôt que par l’impression d’une démonstration réussie.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’approfondit sur les projets : évaluation, conception d’agents, adaptation de modèles, avec l’appui de la communauté AI Engineer. À partir de 2027, l’archétype AI Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle com

jobs.jd: We are looking for an experienced AI/ML Engineer to develop and deploy machine learning solutions for real-world underwater acoustic sensing systems. Optics11 is a deep-tech company developing cutting-edge fiber-optic sensing technologies for challenging environments, including underwater acoustics, offshore energy, and defense applications. Our systems enable high-performance sensing and monitoring through advanced photonics, signal processing, and data-driven intelligence. We are expanding our R&D team with a Senior AI/ML Engineer who combines strong mathematical foundations with applied machine learning expertise to enhance the next generation of intelligent acoustic sensing solutions. You will work closely with acoustics engineers, signal-processing specialists, and embedded/software teams to develop robust ML components that integrate seamlessly into operational systems. This role requires a strong foundation in signal processing, applied mathematics, and statistics, and the ability to combine physics-based acoustic algorithms with data-driven ML methods. Responsibilities: Develop and implement machine learning solutions for underwater acoustic sensing use cases, including detection, classification, localization and anomaly monitoring within fiber-optic sensing systems. Select and adapt modelling approaches based on data availability, operational constraints and system requirements. Apply strong foundations in applied mathematics, statistics and signal processing (e.g., beamforming, spectral analysis, detection pipelines) and integrate these with modern data-driven ML techniques. Design, train, evaluate and benchmark AI/ML models, ensuring robustness, generalization and deployment readiness. Validate models rigorously across laboratory experiments and offshore field datasets, with clear performance tracking and reproducible experimentation. Analyze and interpret large-scale experimental and real-world fiber-optic sensing datasets, contributing to scalable workflows for data preparation, labelling and augmentation. Support technical trade-offs between accuracy, interpretability, latency and real-time or embedded constraints. Collaborate closely with acoustics engineers, signal processing specialists, software and embedded teams to integrate ML components into operational acoustic sensing pipelines. Translate complex AI/ML results into clear technical insights that inform system-level engineering decisions. Contribute to strong engineering practices, including version-controlled experiments, documentation, traceability, validation standards and continuous improvement of ML components. Stay informed about advances in AI/ML for time-series analysis, sensor fusion and signal-informed learning, and prototype promising approaches that complement the broader technology stack. What's in it for you? Competitive salary . Innovative high-tech, international organization . The opportunity to work in a cross-functional and interdisciplinary environment . A lot to learn and to develop, we stimulate personal development . Lunches. Required Qualifications MSc in Machine Learning, Signal Processing, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, Physics, or a related field. Strong foundation in linear algebra, probability, statistics, and signal processing. Supervised and unsupervised learning approaches for detection and classification. Hands-on experience with model training, evaluation, and validation in applied settings. Proficiency in Python and modern ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX). Ability to work in an applied R&D environment with experimental and field data, balancing model performance with real-world constraints. Nice to Have Experience with underwater acoustics, sonar, or beamforming-related applications. Knowledge of embedded or real-time deployment constraints. Experience with sensor fusion, self-supervised learning, or physics-informed ML. Familiarity with offshore, defense, or industrial monitoring domains. Familiarity with structured ML development processes such as CRISP-ML(Q) or similar lifecycle and quality frameworks. jobs.jd:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a Threat Research Engineer, you’ll take ideas from the first question to a working proof of concept, deploy it, and analyze the results yourself. This is a full-stack role, with AI central to how we work. You’ll build agentic workflows for research, analysis, and detection, and use AI tools every day to move faster.

What you’ll do

  • Research new attack surfaces and threat vectors, including AI coding agents, agent plugins, and package ecosystems.
  • Find and responsibly disclose vulnerabilities in open source projects and developer tools.
  • Analyze software supply chain incidents and events.
  • Build AI-powered workflows and agents that automate research, analysis, and detection.
  • Build and maintain the cloud-based systems behind our detection and advisory work.
  • Improve the quality and coverage of our vulnerability and malware advisories.
  • Write up your findings as blog posts and present them at conferences.
  • Take part in on-call or operational support where your team's ownership model requires it.

What you’ll bring

  • Hands-on security experience in research, malware analysis, penetration testing, or security tooling, with both a developer mindset and an adversarial mindset: you can build systems and think about how to break them.
  • Demonstrated experience using AI in real work, such as building with large language model APIs or agent frameworks like LangChain, LangGraph, or agent SDKs.
  • Strong programming skills in Go or Python, with good software engineering practices including testing, code review, continuous integration and continuous delivery, and maintainable code.
  • Experience deploying and running production services on a public cloud.
  • Understanding of how package ecosystems work and how software supply chain attacks happen.
  • Ability to map possible attack vectors, name trade-offs, and make data-driven decisions, balancing quality and speed with customer outcomes in mind while keeping up with security and AI industry trends.
  • Clear writing that explains findings to both engineers and a general audience.
  • Helpful, but not required: published vulnerability findings; security research on AI agents, large language model applications, or Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers; Google Cloud Platform experience; or infrastructure as code experience with Terraform or OpenTofu.

You don’t need deep knowledge of compilers or static application security testing engines. A high-level understanding is enough.

About the team

The Threat Research group researches security threats as they emerge and turns what we learn into protection for GitLab customers. We maintain the GitLab Advisory Database, which powers GitLab’s dependency scanning. We also build detection capabilities, do original vulnerability research, and publish what we find. Recent work includes the Shai-Hulud npm worm and a critical remote code execution vulnerability in Serena, a popular MCP coding agent. You can read more on the Security Labs blog.

jobs.title: ML Hydrologist, Flood Forecasting
jobs.jd: About the Role Global ML flood models now outperform traditional approaches on large rivers, but they still break down in the small, fast catchments where flash floods happen. Riverkin, a VC-backed ETH Zürich Spin-off, is closing that gap. We start from hydrological models trained across thousands of catchments worldwide and make them accurate locally, using a sensor network we deploy ourselves in exactly the places public datasets don't reach. We are looking for an ML hydrologist to own that work. You will report to the CTO and work directly with our other hydrologist, who covers rainfall radar and short-term nowcasting. Why this is interesting Data nobody else has: Our own field-deployed sensors give you live streamflow observations in small, previously ungauged catchments. An open problem: Whether large-sample models can be made reliable at flash-flood scale is unsolved, and you would be working on it with real data and real users. Built to protect lives and critical infrastructure: Your models will power early flood warning systems safeguarding hydropower plants and giving first responders more time to protect communities Publishing and open source: We encourage publishing results and contributing to open tools such as NeuralHydrology and Caravan. Compute: GPU resources are available for training and experimentation. What You'll Do Bring global flood models to the local scale Take state-of-the-art hydrological ML models (LSTMs, Transformers) trained on large-sample datasets and adapt them to the catchments our customers care about. Use our own sensor data alongside public gauge, reanalysis and radar data to fine-tune and validate those models locally. Tackle prediction in ungauged and data-scarce basins through transfer learning and regionalisation. Own hydrological modelling end to end: set the technical direction, decide when to adapt pre-trained models or train our own, and lead the work from experimentation through validation to production. Work as one modelling team Make practical trade-offs between forecast accuracy, model complexity and development effort to build a reliable product that meets customer needs. Work side by side with our hydrologist specialising in rainfall radar and nowcasting to directly integrate rainfall nowcasts into your flood models. Work with software engineers to put models into production and monitor their performance. Identify and test advances in ML flood forecasting, turning promising research into more accurate and reliable forecasts for our customers. Stay close to the real world We believe the best modellers understand the world behind their models. We encourage you to join field deployments and customer conversations to build that understanding firsthand. You are an opinionated contributor to key technical decisions. Who You Are You’ve built and validated hydrological ML models across many catchments and have experience taking modelling work into real-world use. You combine scientific rigour with product judgement: you test assumptions, understand uncertainty and focus on improvements that matter to customers. You take ownership from an open question to a working solution. You set priorities, make decisions and keep moving without waiting for perfect information. You care deeply about the quality of your work. You dig into why models fail, follow problems through and stay invested in how your forecasts perform after deployment. You communicate clearly in writing and in person, can explain your reasoning and trade-offs, and work closely with people across hydrology, software, hardware and field operations. Technical Requirements MSc or PhD in hydrology, water resources, or atmospheric sciences . Hands-on experience training or fine-tuning ML streamflow or flood models across many catchments at once (regional, continental or global), for example on CAMELS or Caravan. Experience with single-catchment models alone is not sufficient. Experience transferring such models to new or data-scarce catchments through fine-tuning, regionalisation, or prediction in ungauged basins. Strong understanding of rainfall-runoff processes and the limitations of hydrological observations and input data. Experience validating models across unseen catchments and time periods, including assessing flood-peak magnitude, timing and predictive uncertainty. Strong Python skills, with experience writing maintainable code for data processing, modelling and reproducible experiments. Practical depth in deep learning for time series, including developing, training and debugging models in PyTorch or a comparable framework. Nice to Have Publications or open-source work on large-sample hydrology, transfer learning, or ungauged-basin prediction. Experience with NeuralHydrology, ERA5 or similar global forcing datasets. Experience with sub-daily or event-based flood modelling. Experience processing large hydrometeorological datasets with tools such as xarray and Dask, and formats such as Zarr. Previous early startup experience. Role Details Contract: Permanent, full-time (100% FTE). Start date: immediately Reports to : CTO. Compensation : Commensurate with experience + equity Growth : a key early hire with the opportunity to shape Riverkin's flood modelling as the team grows. Location: Four days per week in our Zurich office and one day working from home. Work authorisation : Swiss or EU/EFTA citizenship, or a valid Swiss work permit, is required.
